evidence: Cic. de Or. 3.39: ōrātōrēs et poētae (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The ordinary word in prose and verse. In Plautus also a contriver, a schemer (Lewis & Short).
First a seer or prophet; the old name for a poet, fallen out of use until Vergil restored it to honour (Lewis & Short). The poet as inspired singer, not the everyday word.

phrases.latin: meminī super Pindarō poētā et Vergiliō in hunc fermē modum disserere
phrases.english: I remember him talking about Pindar the poet and Vergil roughly like this

phrases.latin: etiam dicta clārōrum virōrum et ēlēctōs ex poētīs maximē … locōs ēdiscere inter lūsum licet
phrases.english: even sayings of famous men and passages chosen mostly from the poets can be learned by heart while playing
